proposals.before: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou closed Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.
proposals.after: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou raised a mound over Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.
proposals.reason: In 武王封比干之墓, the transmitted gloss 積土為封 explains heaping earth over the tomb; “closed” wrongly suggests sealing the tomb rather than the commemorative mound action.

decisions.reason: The Jin shu states that King Wu acted on Bi Gan's tomb; the parallel Shiji Music Treatise preserves Zheng Xuan's gloss that this was heaping earth. The revised wording expresses that sense without adding a date or physical details.

sourceWitness.citation: Shiji Music Treatise, Zheng Xuan gloss, https://www.xuoda.com/ls/shiji2/102.htm
sourceWitness.excerpt: 封王子比干之墓，〔集解〕鄭玄曰：「積土為封。封比干之墓，崇賢也。」
